data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Biological evolution has no conscious aim, whereas Popperian science has the explicit normative aim of truth","Survival in nature is immediate and reproductive, while corroboration in science is retrospective and logical","Evolutionary fitness is relative to an environment, while scientific truth is intended to be absolute (or closer to it)"],"overturn_conditions":["If it can be shown that survival in evolution implies a probabilistic increase in future survival rates in a way that corroboration does not for theories.","If the normative aim of truth in science is proven to be incoherent without a probabilistic foundation."],"shared_structure":["Selection mechanism operates without guaranteeing future success","Past performance is used as a filter, not a predictor of probability","The system aims for an ideal (truth/survival) without claiming to have reached it"],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_003"],"transfer_claims":["Just as we prefer organisms that have survived severe environmental tests without assuming they are immortal, we prefer theories that have survived severe tests without assuming they are probable.","The rationality of the preference lies in the rigor of the test, not in the statistical likelihood of the outcome."]},"claim":"Popper's preference for better-corroborated theories is defensible on his own terms not as an inductive inference of truth, but as a non-inductive methodological rule grounded in the aim of science to find true theories with high content; however, accepting this defense costs the ability to claim that such preferences make a theory 'more likely' to be true in any probabilistic sense, forcing a strict separation between rational action and epistemic probability.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the Miller-Tich\u00fd refutation of verisimilitude is taken as final and exhaustive, then Popper has no non-inductive bridge between corroboration and truth-likeness, rendering the preference irrational on his own strict logical terms.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If 'rational defensibility' is defined strictly as requiring a increase in logical probability, then Popper's preference fails by definition, as he explicitly denies corroboration increases probability.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the practical necessity of acting on the best-corroborated theory is conflated with a logical justification for its truth, the argument collapses into the very induction Popper rejected.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The argument proceeds by distinguishing between the logical status of a theory (which remains unprobabilized by tests) and the procedural rationality of choosing the theory that has best withstood attempts at falsification. It leverages Popper's concept of 'verisimilitude' (truth-likeness) cautiously, acknowledging the Miller-Tich\u00fd critique but arguing that Popper's later appeal to 'corroboration as a guide to verisimilitude' functions as a metaphysical hope or regulative ideal rather than a formal logic, thereby avoiding the smuggling of induction while admitting a gap in formal justification.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
